title: Pinning enforcement state machine + escalation scripts (operator playbook)
body:
Purpose:
This is an operator-focused playbook that defines the enforcement state machine for tenant region pins, the observability triggers that move tenants between states, and canned escalation scripts for on-call and account teams. Goal: make pin transitions deterministic, auditable and actionable for SREs and support engineers during enforcement rollouts.

Scope / assumptions:
- Applies to private deployments and Dedicated customers who have region pin requirements. Hosted enforcement is covered separately.
- We assume tenant metadata (tenant_id, requested_region, legal_tag, pin_effective_ts) is canonical in the residency service (residency-db).
- This doc covers enforcement states, transition triggers, operator actions, evidence collection, and rollback paths.
- Not a policy doc — legal policy remains source-of-truth in contract clauses. This is how ops enforces.

High-level state machine (names intentionally explicit for operator UI):
- REQUESTED: Customer/contract/CS requested a region pin but no enforcement started.
- VALIDATING: System is collecting evidence (KMS location check, dataset anchors, routing table readiness). Manual checks can be required.
- SOFT_PINNED: Routing annotated to prefer requested region, but cross-region fallbacks allowed for throughput events. Telemetry visible and 1 week observation window.
- HARD_PINNED: Enforcement active – all tenant serving and storage must be anchored to requested region. Cross-region calls are rejected or routed to exceptions flow.
- GRACE_PERIOD: Temporary state after an enforcement failure: allow short-lived cross-region fallthrough while operator remediates.
- EVICTED: Pin removed by policy or system (rare) — requires customer notification and postmortem.
- EXCEPTION_REQUESTED: Operator/CS opens a temporary exception to allow a specific flow cross-region.
- EXCEPTION_APPROVED: Exception recorded with TTL and audit tag.

Example transitions and triggers (with telemetry rules):
- REQUESTED -> VALIDATING: Triggered when contract flag set + onboarding checklist created. No telemetry requirement.
- VALIDATING -> SOFT_PINNED: All validation checks pass: residency-db shows anchors present, KMS keys region match, region-edge caches report >95% local hits for baseline test traffic.
- SOFT_PINNED -> HARD_PINNED: After observation window (configurable, default 7 days) with no >1% cross-region error rate and performance SLOs met.
- HARD_PINNED -> GRACE_PERIOD: Triggered if the global cross-region rejection rate for tenant >0.5% for 10m OR key infra alerts (eg region-edge node OOM) occur.
- GRACE_PERIOD -> HARD_PINNED: If remediation actions clear and telemetry drops below thresholds within grace TTL.
- ANY_STATE -> EXCEPTION_REQUESTED: Manual action by operator/CS via internal UI or ticket.
- EXCEPTION_APPROVED -> previous state: After TTL expiry or manual revoke.

Telemetry signals and thresholds (initial proposals):
- Local-hit ratio (edge cache): threshold 95% for promotion to HARD_PINNED.
- Cross-region call rejection rate: if >0.5% over 10m, consider entering GRACE_PERIOD.
- Latency delta (local vs fallback): if fallback adds >200ms p50 and increases error rates, trigger validation failure.
- Missing-anchor alert: if residency-db shows >0 missing anchors for critical tenant resources, fail VALIDATING.
- Audit-ops gap: missing audit evidence for a pinned tenant should block HARD_PINNED promotion.

Operator checklist for key transitions (copy/paste friendly):
- To promote to SOFT_PINNED:
  1) Confirm residency-db entries: SELECT * FROM residency.tenants WHERE tenant_id = '<tenant>' AND requested_region = '<region>'.
  2) Run anchor-check script: tools/anchors/check_anchor.sh <tenant> <region> -> expect exit 0.
  3) Confirm KMS key region via kms-api: GET /v1/keys/<key> -> region == <region>.
  4) Post note on ticket with evidence hashes and set state=SOFT_PINNED in UI.

- To promote to HARD_PINNED:
  1) Ensure soft window completed (default 7d) and telemetry snapshot attached.
  2) Run simulation: infra/simulate/region_pin_test --tenant <tenant> --duration 300s -> attach log.
  3) Approve with SLA owner + CS. Update residency-db state and notify customer (template below).

- Hard failure / GRACE_PERIOD entry remediation script (operator):
  1) Immediately declare GRACE_PERIOD for tenant (set TTL 15m by default).
  2) Post Slack incident to #residency-ops with template (see below).
  3) Roll back recent config changes (if any) and re-route traffic to a safe fallback pool.
  4) Collect pcap/traces for offending flows and attach to JIRA incident.
  5) Escalate to infra team if node-level OOM or network partition is present.

Canned Slack/Email templates (operator -> internal)
- Incident post to #residency-ops:
  [ALERT] GRACE_PERIOD declared for tenant <tenant_id> (region=<region>) at <ts>
  Reason: cross-region rejection rate exceeded 0.5% (10m) / node OOM
  Current impact: % of requests failing, approximate user-facing latency increase
  Action: running anchor-check + sim, assigned to @<oncall>, paging infra if needed

- Customer notification (CS template):
  Subject: Temporary grace window for regional pin enforcement for <tenant_name>
  Body: We detected elevated failures related to your region pin for <region>. To prevent wider service impact we have temporarily enabled a short grace window to allow in-flight traffic to continue while we investigate. We will follow up within <ETA>.

Exception workflow (short-lived cross-region allowances):
- Create EXCEPTION ticket: include justification, flows, TTL, and owner. Tag with legal_tag and audit_hash.
- Record exception in residency-db with exception_id and expiry_ts.
- Telemetry must include exception_id on all cross-region flows while exception active.
- Post-ttl: system auto-revokes and emits evidence bundle for audit.

Evidence collection (minimum required for audits):
- audit_manifest.json (sha256) listing: tenant_id, pin_state, operator_id, timestamp, linked KMS key ids, anchor artifact ids, exception_ids.
- Traffic snapshot (start/end ts) including request headers for sample size up to 500 reqs. Redact PII.
- Config diff on promotion time: git diff between routing config commits.

Playbook runbook examples (quick commands):
- Check current state: curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://residency-api.internal/v1/tenants/<tenant>/state
- Force set state (operator only): POST to /v1/tenants/<tenant>/state {\"state\":\"SOFT_PINNED\",\"operator\":\"a.kumar\",\"note\":\"test promotion\"}
- Run anchor probe: python tools/anchor_probe.py --tenant <tenant> --region <region> --out /tmp/probe.json

Testing scenarios (for release/ops drills):
- Scenario A (gradual pin): run soft promotion, inject 2% synthetic cross-region traffic for 24h -> verify system stays SOFT and does not auto-promote to HARD until baseline passes.
- Scenario B (failure during HARD): create node OOM on one zone, measure detection and auto-grace TTL behavior.
- Scenario C (exception TTL expiry): grant exception for 1h, confirm traces include exception_id and system revokes correctly.

Open questions / design tradeoffs (needs product/legal signoff):
- Default thresholds: conservative (0.5%) vs. permissive (1%). Lower threshold reduces incorrect HARD promotions but increases operational churn.
- TTL durations for GRACE_PERIOD and EXCEPTION_APPROVED. Proposed defaults: GRACE 15m, EXCEPTION 1h.
- How strictly to enforce storage vs serving anchors (some customers allow storage in region A while serving in region B). Need contract mapping.

Next actions (short list):
- [ ] Sync with Legal on required audit_manifest fields (owner: Mariana). Due: 2024-12-01.
- [ ] Add state machine to residency UI mockups (owner: Jonas). Due: 2024-11-21.
- [ ] Implement telemetry rules as alerting policies in AlertManager stub (owner: DevOncall). Due: 2024-12-08.

Appendix: evidence checklist (quick)
- audit_manifest.json attached? Y/N
- anchor_probe result attached? Y/N
- KMS region confirmed? Y/N
- exception_id present (if applicable)? Y/N
- customer notified (CS ticket id)? Y/N

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add sample SQL queries for anchor validation (TODO @Jonas).
- Wire up auto-evidence bundle generation on state transitions (low priority).
- Add runbook for hosted-tier (separate doc)

If you are the oncall and you get paged: treat any HARD_PINNED failure as high-priority. Follow the GRACE_PERIOD script first to reduce customer impact, then escalate systemic issues to infra and product.

-- a.kumar (draft)
